item.text:
**4B.3 Research Note**
**Working verdict:** **mixed, leaning no**. Marcos’s 2024 public posture was more permissive than Duterte-era norms in some places, but the record still shows persistent red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats against journalists, activists, and labor organizers. I found no strong 2024 evidence that he openly welcomed opposition victories or robust civil-society scrutiny.

| Direction | Claim-level item | Source | Date | URL | QIDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Marcos told critics to let Comelec handle allegations that signatures in the people’s initiative drive may have been bought. That is a small but real sign of deference to the election body rather than direct executive interference. | GMA News Online | 2024-01-23 | https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/895067/marcos-on-people-s-initiative-for-cha-cha-let-comelec-do-their-job/story/ | 4B.3, 4B.2, 4B.1 |
| Positive | Marcos publicly pledged a free and safe environment for journalists and said critical press is better than cooperative press. That supports tolerance for criticism and investigative reporting at the level of rhetoric. | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-15 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-declares-free-safe-environment-for-journalists-under-bagong-pilipinas/ | 4B.3, 4B.2, 4B.1, 3B.8 |
| Positive | The government said DICT and the NSC were investigating a manipulated deepfake video and considering legal action. This is a legal/institutional response rather than an obvious censorship sweep. | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-26 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-vows-legal-action-vs-deep-fake-video-creators-spreaders/ | 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8 |
| Positive | Freedom House says elections are free from overt restrictions, even though disinformation, vote buying, and red-tagging distort competition. That leaves some room for opposition participation, but not a clean tolerance finding. | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024 | 4B.3, 4B.1, 4B.2 |
| Positive / mixed | The Supreme Court issued a ruling rejecting red-tagging as a threat to life, liberty, and security. In the record I found, Marcos did not retaliate against that judicial constraint, which slightly favors a permissive reading. | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-08 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/08/philippines-supreme-court-rejects-red-tagging | 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8 |
| Negative | HRW said red-tagging under Marcos placed leftist activists and critics at serious risk, with officials and supporters accusing them of communist ties. That is directly inconsistent with tolerating robust opposition and monitoring. | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/philippines-red-tagging-puts-activists-risk | 4B.3, 4B.1, 4B.2, 3B.8 |
| Negative | The Reuters Institute report says red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats against journalists persisted under Marcos. That points to a coercive information environment that chills criticism and investigative reporting. | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines | 4B.3, 4B.1, 4B.2, 3B.8 |
| Negative | HRW reported Marcos-era officials and police or military members repeatedly visited union leaders and threatened them by linking them to communism. That is direct intimidation of civil-society organization. | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-25 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders | 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.7 |
| Negative | HRW’s 2025 report on 2024 says red-tagging, killings, disappearances, and political violence persisted, with violence against local officials increasing ahead of the 2025 midterms. That suggests the political field remained coercive rather than broadly open. | Human Rights Watch | 2025-01-16 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/philippines | 4B.3, 4B.1, 4B.2, 3B.10 |
| Negative | Freedom House says red-tagging persisted and that disinformation and vote buying undermined fair competition. That undercuts a claim that Marcos genuinely tolerated full opposition contestation. | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024 | 4B.3, 4B.1, 4B.2 |

**Bottom line:** Marcos showed some institutional tolerance for criticism and watchdog roles, but the 2024 record still contains sustained intimidation of activists, labor leaders, journalists, and other critical voices. That is not a clean acceptance of opposition, satire, protest, or civil-society monitoring.

**Search gap:** I did not find a concrete 2024 case where Marcos clearly accepted an opposition electoral victory, nor a specific source on tolerance of satire. The evidence is strongest on journalism and civil-society monitoring, and weaker on direct treatment of opposition wins because 2024 had no major national opposition victory to test.
